newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks follow battered Wall St down.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks follow battered Wall St down.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended weaker after North American markets were battered by Greenspan's warnings of overheated equities. * Bargain hunters managed to bring Toronto up from lows.

Toronto stocks closed weaker on Wednesday, hit by the wave of selling after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan questioned whether equity prices could sustain their strong two-year growth spurt.
"It's bearish for stocks," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie.
The Toronto stock market's key 300 Composite Index ended 46.35 points down at 6201.43 after earlier losing as much as 61 points.
Greenspan also expressed concern about the risks of inflation and warned the Fed may need to hike interest rates.
Greenspan sparked a similar sell-off in December after remarking on the "irrational exuberance" of the stock market, but North American markets later recovered.
"We're going to continue to get this kind of sell-off and bargain-hunting," Beattie said.
Wednesday's trading was brisk with volume of 104.9 million shares worth C$1.88 billion.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices tumbled, led by golds, transportation, consumer products and base metals.
Declining issues outnumbered advances 595 to 408 while another 287 stocks were unchanged.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Bank stocks lost ground after strong gains on Tuesday. The Bank of Nova Scotia fell 0.30 to close at 52.60 on nearly 2.3 million shares, while the Bank of Montreal lost 0.45 to finish at 49.05 on 1.4 million shares.
* Canadian Natural Resources Ltd jumped 1.05 to 34 in heavy trading after brokerage Goldman Sachs started coverage of the energy firm and added it to its recommended list.
